page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate balanced performance across standard compute workloads. The instance achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1926.0 and a multi-core score of 7695.0. In stress-ng tests, single-core performance reached 1899.38 and multi-core reached 7550.03, both placing in the average tier. Notably, the CPU features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which support accelerated vector and matrix operations. Single-threaded gzip compression performance is strong at 32.73 GB/sec, and text processing benchmarks also show strong results. However, memory performance is a relative bottleneck, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the bottom 25% and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured at 47.98 GB/sec. Large-model LLM text generation is slow, yielding 6.32 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7i.2xlarge offers a high-density compute profile with DDR5 memory, making it suitable for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. The absence of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes, which may impact overall I/O-heavy workloads. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and data compression tasks.
